A_target.statement:
Let $X$ be a [[Definition:Continuous Random Variable|continuous random variable]] with [[Definition:Probability Density Function|density]] $p$.
The [[Definition:Differential Entropy|differential entropy]] of $X$ is:
:$\displaystyle \map h X = -\int_{-\infty}^\infty \map p x \log \map p x \rd x$

B_source.statement:
Let $X$ be a [[Definition:Discrete Random Variable|discrete random variable]] taking values $x_i$ with probabilities $p_i$.
The [[Definition:Entropy (Information Theory)|Shannon entropy]] of $X$ is:
:$\displaystyle \map H X = -\sum_i p_i \log p_i$

substitutions.the discrete outcome i: a bin of width Delta on the real line
substitutions.the probability mass p_i: the mass p(x_i) Delta of that bin

derived.the divergent term log(1/Delta): the additive constant that must be discarded

object_map.reformulation: Discrete entropy must first be split into a Riemann-sum part and a resolution-dependent part before a limit can be taken at all.

validity_conditions: the density p must be Riemann integrable for the bin sums to converge
the quantity H(X^Delta) + log Delta must converge, which is why differential entropy is only defined up to the discarded divergence
unlike discrete entropy, the limit can be negative, so nonnegativity does not transfer
proof_plan: Quantize $X$ into bins $\hointr {i \Delta} {\paren {i + 1} \Delta}$ of width $\Delta$, and let $X^\Delta$ be the bin index.

By the [[Mean Value Theorem for Integrals]], there exists $x_i$ in bin $i$ with:
:$\map \Pr {X^\Delta = i} = \map p {x_i} \Delta$

Discard the divergent term $\log \dfrac 1 \Delta$ and let $\Delta \to 0$:
:$\map H {X^\Delta} + \log \Delta \to \map h X$
